name: Xenagos
description: Xenagos is a satyr planeswalker of the Skola Valley on Theros, Raissa's son, who became the god of revels.

description_citations.text: "Xenagos". Magic: The Gathering story profiles, Wizards of the Coast.
"Thank the Gods" by Clayton Kroh. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 30 Apr 2014.
"Kruphix's Insight" by Kelly Digges. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 11 Jun 2014.

summary.text: Xenagos is a satyr planeswalker of the Skola Valley on Theros, Raissa's son, who became the god of revels.

citations.text: "Xenagos". Magic: The Gathering story profiles, Wizards of the Coast.
"Thank the Gods" by Clayton Kroh. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 30 Apr 2014.
"Kruphix's Insight" by Kelly Digges. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 11 Jun 2014.

bio.text: Raissa gives birth to her horned son, and a vision shows him grown and destined to be a king.

citations.text: "Thank the Gods" by Clayton Kroh. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 30 Apr 2014.
"Thank the Gods" by Clayton Kroh. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 30 Apr 2014.

bio.text: As a six-year-old he sets her bed alight, and they have been cast out of Setessa after he pushed a council member's son to his death.

citations.text: "Thank the Gods" by Clayton Kroh. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 30 Apr 2014.

bio.text: In the vision the constellations of Nyx turn on him with outrage and he rises to meet them, laughing, with the starfish impaled on his stick.

citations.text: "Thank the Gods" by Clayton Kroh. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 30 Apr 2014.
"Thank the Gods" by Clayton Kroh. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 30 Apr 2014.

bio.text: His planeswalker spark ignites and he is excited to bring his hedonism to distant planes, but finds only disillusionment in seeking all the pleasures of the Multiverse.

citations.text: "Xenagos". Magic: The Gathering story profiles, Wizards of the Coast.
"Xenagos". Magic: The Gathering story profiles, Wizards of the Coast.

bio.text: Kruphix explains that Xenagos traveled to godless worlds and tried to show everyone the gods were a lie, but people saw only chaos.

citations.text: "Kruphix's Insight" by Kelly Digges. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 11 Jun 2014.

bio.text: Xenagos becomes a god, and Elspeth, with Ajani, uses Godsend to cut him from the sky.

citations.text: "Kruphix's Insight" by Kelly Digges. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 11 Jun 2014.
"Kruphix's Insight" by Kelly Digges. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 11 Jun 2014.

status.text: Xenagos is dead, killed by Elspeth, and a later page describes him as a foe Elspeth and Ajani fought and slew at Nyx.

citations.text: "Kruphix's Insight" by Kelly Digges. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 11 Jun 2014.
"Kruphix's Insight" by Kelly Digges. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 11 Jun 2014.

timeline.summary: Elspeth strikes down Xenagos in Nyx.
timeline.quote: the pair battled the god until at last Elspeth struck him down

citation.text: "Ajani Goldmane", section "Journey to Theros". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Xenagos besieges Akros with minotaurs and the Akroans capture him.
timeline.quote: Queen Cymede informed them that the Akroans had captured the satyr Xenagos

citation.text: "Akros", section "The rise and fall of Xenagos". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Xenagos uses the victory celebration to stage the Great Revel and ascend to godhood.
timeline.quote: Xenagos used the occasion to stage the Great Revel , the final ritual that propelled him to godhood

citation.text: "Akros", section "The rise and fall of Xenagos". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Xenagos controls Elspeth; she kills the Obliterator in her memory and realizes she has killed Daxos.
timeline.quote: only realizing too late that she had just killed Daxos

citation.text: "Elspeth Tirel", section "The Great Revel". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Heliod turns against Elspeth, believing she was part of Xenagos's plan.
timeline.quote: Heliod was wroth, believing she was implicit in Xenagos's plan, and sought to destroy her.

citation.text: "Elspeth Tirel", section "The Great Revel". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: After Elspeth slays Xenagos, Heliod has Daxos remove traces of other gods from Meletis; the gods go to war, rifts open to the Underworld, and Erebos neglects the souls under his charge out of hatred of Heliod.
timeline.quote: He hated Heliod most of all, and in his rage, he neglected to keep a tight grip on the souls under his purview.

citation.text: "Erebos", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Heliod blames Elspeth for Xenagos' apotheosis and tries unsuccessfully to kill her.
timeline.quote: Heliod was quick to blame Elspeth and once again tried to kill her, but failed.

citation.text: "Heliod", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: After Elspeth's battle with Xenagos in Nyx, Heliod takes Godsend and stabs her, murdering her while taunting her.
timeline.quote: taking Godsend away from her and stabbing her with it

citation.text: "Heliod", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Elspeth Tirel kills Xenagos.
timeline.quote: God of Revels. Killed by Elspeth Tirel .

citation.text: "List of deities", section "Minor gods". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: In 4559 AR Xenagos gathers monsters to attack Meletis, Akros and Setessa, causing the Silence of the Gods.
timeline.quote: These attacks became so severe that the gods themselves went blind

citation.text: "Meletis", section "The rise and fall of Xenagos". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Xenagos ascends to godhood during the siege of Akros and Elspeth is scapegoated and exiled.
timeline.quote: In circumstances largely under mystery , Xenagos managed to ascend to godhood.

citation.text: "Meletis", section "The rise and fall of Xenagos". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: During the Silence of the Gods, Xenagos ascends through the Great Revel and imprisons Nylea in beast form.
timeline.quote: imprisoning Nylea in the form of a beast within her domain

citation.text: "Nylea", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Elspeth and Ajani free Nylea in Nyx, and Elspeth slays Xenagos with an arrow Nylea struck.
timeline.quote: The pair freed her from her magical prison, restoring her true form

citation.text: "Nylea", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Phenax covertly supports Xenagos's apotheosis to subvert divine authority.
timeline.quote: He covertly supported Xenagos's apotheosis

citation.text: "Phenax", section "Divine Relationships". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: In her vision the boy crowds out and eclipses the girl; Raissa breaches the vision and afterward feels only one child within her.
timeline.quote: feeling only the presence of one child within her.

citation.text: "Raissa", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: At eight months the starfish shows Raissa places beyond Theros that her child will visit.
timeline.quote: Other planes of existence her child would visit.

citation.text: "Raissa", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Xenagos is born, kicking and horned; the midwife curses him and leaves in a huff.
timeline.quote: when the midwife finally pulled him from her, he kicked at her.

citation.text: "Raissa", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Raissa decides not to abandon her son as most satyr women do, believing he is special and needs her.
timeline.quote: But Raissa looked down at the pink face of her boy and knew she could not.

citation.text: "Raissa", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Six years later Xenagos shoves a council member's son to his death from a rope bridge, so they are cast out of Setessa.
timeline.quote: He had caused them to be cast out of Setessa

citation.text: "Raissa", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Xenagos sets his mother's bed alight and hits her on the head with a stick, giggling.
timeline.quote: he struck her in the side of her head with his stick.

citation.text: "Raissa", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Raissa revisits the starfish and sees the constellations of Nyx turn on her son in outrage and advance with storms.
timeline.quote: They faced Raissa's son, and outrage flared in their eyes.

citation.text: "Raissa", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The vision ends with Xenagos laughing and holding a stick dripping ichor, the starfish impaled on it.
timeline.quote: At the end of the stick writhed the impaled gray body of the starfish.

citation.text: "Raissa", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Xenagos's planeswalker spark ignites and he leaves Theros, later returning with a desire for power.
timeline.quote: until his planeswalker spark ignited and he was able to travel away from Theros

citation.text: "Theros", section "Xenagos". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Xenagos resolves to enter the Therosian pantheon as a god.
timeline.quote: his mission now is to enter the Therosian pantheon as a god

citation.text: "Theros", section "Xenagos". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Xenagos attacks the poleis with otherworldly monsters, blinding the gods, and Kruphix enacts the Silence of the Gods.
timeline.quote: Kruphix then enacted the Silence of the Gods

citation.text: "Theros (plane)", section "The rise and fall of Xenagos". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Xenagos ascends to godhood through the forced worship of a Great Revel after the siege of Akros, and Elspeth is scapegoated and exiled.
timeline.quote: Using the forced worhsip of mortal revelers, Xenagos managed to ascend to godhood.

citation.text: "Theros (plane)", section "The rise and fall of Xenagos". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Elspeth throws her spear into Xenagos' chest, exploding the arrowhead Nylea shot into him and killing him.
timeline.quote: Elspeth managed to throw the spear into Xenagos's chest

citation.text: "Theros (plane)", section "The rise and fall of Xenagos". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Xenagos ascends to godhood and is killed by Elspeth, revealing that the gods are replaceable.
timeline.quote: Xenagos ascended to godhood and was killed by Elspeth Tirel

citation.text: "War of the Gods", section "Description". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Xenagos's spark ignited during the Bakkeia and he became a planeswalker.
timeline.quote: this lifestyle led to his ascension, his spark igniting during the Bakkeia.

citation.text: "Xenagos", section "The Rise of King Stranger". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Xenagos returned to Theros and attacked Meletis, Akros and Setessa with otherworldly monsters, blinding the gods.
timeline.quote: These attacks became so severe that the gods themselves began to go blind, cut off from their oracles.

citation.text: "Xenagos", section "Return to Theros". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: After a Great Revel following the siege of Akros, Xenagos ascended to godhood as god of revels, and Elspeth was scapegoated for Daxos's death and exiled.
timeline.quote: Xenagos held the position of the god of the revels, furthering the chaos and distrust of the established pantheon.

citation.text: "Xenagos", section "Return to Theros". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Elspeth and Ajani arrived in Nyx, and Xenagos knocked Elspeth down.
timeline.quote: Elspeth and her friend Ajani arrived in Nyx to set Theros right again.

citation.text: "Xenagos", section "Deicide in Nyx". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Elspeth threw Godsend into Xenagos's chest, detonating Nylea's arrowhead and killing him in Nyx.
timeline.quote: Elspeth managed to throw the spear into Xenagos's chest

citation.text: "Xenagos", section "Deicide in Nyx". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Xenagos returns to Theros and performs rituals to become god of revels, blurring the line between Nyx and the mortal world.
timeline.quote: These rituals had an unanticipated side effect: the blurring of the lines between the realm of the gods and everyday existence.

citation.work: Planeswalker's Guide to Born of the Gods
citation.text: "Planeswalker's Guide to Born of the Gods". Uncharted Realms, Wizards of the Coast, 8 Jan 2014. Archived by the Internet Archive.

timeline.summary: Elspeth leads an army of heroes from Akros, Meletis and Setessa to break the siege; the victory celebration becomes the ritual that launches Xenagos into Nyx as a god.
timeline.quote: the victory celebration after the battle became the ultimate ritual to launch Xenagos into Nyx as a god.

citation.work: Planeswalker's Guide to Born of the Gods
citation.text: "Planeswalker's Guide to Born of the Gods". Uncharted Realms, Wizards of the Coast, 8 Jan 2014. Archived by the Internet Archive.

timeline.summary: Elspeth is blamed for Xenagos's ascension and driven into the wilderness, vanishing in disgrace.
timeline.quote: Elspeth was blamed for his ascension and driven into the wilderness.

citation.work: Planeswalker's Guide to Born of the Gods
citation.text: "Planeswalker's Guide to Born of the Gods". Uncharted Realms, Wizards of the Coast, 8 Jan 2014. Archived by the Internet Archive.

timeline.summary: The gods realize a mortal has forced his way into the pantheon and fear their nature as creations of the world being revealed.
timeline.quote: a mortal has launched himself into Nyx and forced his way into the pantheon

citation.work: Planeswalker's Guide to Born of the Gods
citation.text: "Planeswalker's Guide to Born of the Gods". Uncharted Realms, Wizards of the Coast, 8 Jan 2014. Archived by the Internet Archive.

timeline.summary: Xenagos returns to Theros to become the god of revels as the boundary with Nyx thins and Nyxborn pour into the mortal world.
timeline.quote: the planeswalker Xenagos returns to Theros to become the god of revels.

citation.text: "Born of the Gods", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The victory celebration becomes the ritual that launches Xenagos into Nyx as a god; Elspeth is blamed and driven away.
timeline.quote: Elspeth is blamed for his ascension and driven away in disgrace.

citation.text: "Born of the Gods", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Akroans defeat Mogis's minotaur horde and celebrate; Xenagos uses the occasion for his final ritual of ascension to godhood.
timeline.quote: Xenagos used the occasion to stage the final ritual that propelled him to godhood.

citation.work: Planeswalker's Guide to Journey into Nyx
citation.text: "Planeswalker's Guide to Journey into Nyx". Uncharted Realms, Wizards of the Coast, 2 Apr 2014. Archived by the Internet Archive.

timeline.summary: The gods blame mortals and swear vengeance against human civilization.
timeline.quote: they swore vengeance against human civilization

citation.work: Planeswalker's Guide to Journey into Nyx
citation.text: "Planeswalker's Guide to Journey into Nyx". Uncharted Realms, Wizards of the Coast, 2 Apr 2014. Archived by the Internet Archive.

timeline.summary: Elspeth and Ajani prepare to face Xenagos in Nyx, Elspeth armed with Godsend.
timeline.quote: Now Elspeth and Ajani face Xenagos on his home ground.

citation.work: Planeswalker's Guide to Journey into Nyx
citation.text: "Planeswalker's Guide to Journey into Nyx". Uncharted Realms, Wizards of the Coast, 2 Apr 2014. Archived by the Internet Archive.

timeline.summary: Xenagos, jaded satyr-king, broods over the revel and recalls how his spark ignited and showed him other worlds.
timeline.quote: But once his spark ignited, he'd seen beyond the boundaries of Theros, and everything he thought he knew had been shattered.

citation.work: Theros eBook Godsend , Part 1: Sample Chapter
citation.text: "Theros eBook Godsend , Part 1: Sample Chapter". Uncharted Realms, Wizards of the Coast, 2 Apr 2014. Archived by the Internet Archive.

timeline.summary: Xenagos uses fiery magic to force the crowd to laugh uproariously at his jest.
timeline.quote: A fiery light flashed in his eyes, and the audience began to laugh uproariously at his jest.

citation.work: Theros eBook Godsend , Part 1: Sample Chapter
citation.text: "Theros eBook Godsend , Part 1: Sample Chapter". Uncharted Realms, Wizards of the Coast, 2 Apr 2014. Archived by the Internet Archive.

timeline.summary: Xenagos casts a vine dome over the valley to block the gods' sight, wary of Nylea.
timeline.quote: a thicket of ethereal vines crawled over the valley and settled like a living dome above them all

citation.work: Theros eBook Godsend , Part 1: Sample Chapter
citation.text: "Theros eBook Godsend , Part 1: Sample Chapter". Uncharted Realms, Wizards of the Coast, 2 Apr 2014. Archived by the Internet Archive.

timeline.summary: Xenagos ensnares three dancers with capture-magic and picks Deiphon to tell a god-story.
timeline.quote: But the young man was more interesting.

citation.work: Theros eBook Godsend , Part 1: Sample Chapter
citation.text: "Theros eBook Godsend , Part 1: Sample Chapter". Uncharted Realms, Wizards of the Coast, 2 Apr 2014. Archived by the Internet Archive.

timeline.summary: Deiphon tells Xenagos that Callaphe the Mariner has returned.
timeline.quote: "Callaphe the Mariner has returned," Deiphon said triumphantly

citation.work: Theros eBook Godsend , Part 1: Sample Chapter
citation.text: "Theros eBook Godsend , Part 1: Sample Chapter". Uncharted Realms, Wizards of the Coast, 2 Apr 2014. Archived by the Internet Archive.

timeline.summary: Xenagos interrupts and mocks the god-story, breaching storytelling etiquette.
timeline.quote: "And blah, blah, blah, Kruphix slapped their hands and told them to never do it again or they'd be sealed into Nyx like bad children," Xenagos quipped.

citation.work: Theros eBook Godsend , Part 1: Sample Chapter
citation.text: "Theros eBook Godsend , Part 1: Sample Chapter". Uncharted Realms, Wizards of the Coast, 2 Apr 2014. Archived by the Internet Archive.

timeline.summary: Xenagos, enraged when Deiphon tries to leave, raises a red mist that compels the revelers to dance and gather stones.
timeline.quote: A red mist rose up out of the enchanted ground and shimmered around the legs of the revelers.

citation.work: Theros eBook Godsend , Part 1: Sample Chapter
citation.text: "Theros eBook Godsend , Part 1: Sample Chapter". Uncharted Realms, Wizards of the Coast, 2 Apr 2014. Archived by the Internet Archive.

timeline.summary: Xenagos knocks Deiphon off the platform; entranced, Deiphon dances.
timeline.quote: Slamming his fist against Deiphon's skull, Xenagos knocked the young man off the edge and to the ground.

citation.work: Theros eBook Godsend , Part 1: Sample Chapter
citation.text: "Theros eBook Godsend , Part 1: Sample Chapter". Uncharted Realms, Wizards of the Coast, 2 Apr 2014. Archived by the Internet Archive.

timeline.summary: The entranced satyrs stone Deiphon, who dies smiling and fatally wounded.
timeline.quote: Another joined in and then another, until the rocks rained down on him.

citation.work: Theros eBook Godsend , Part 1: Sample Chapter
citation.text: "Theros eBook Godsend , Part 1: Sample Chapter". Uncharted Realms, Wizards of the Coast, 2 Apr 2014. Archived by the Internet Archive.

timeline.summary: Keranos's lightning breaches Xenagos's vine-roof, scattering the revelers.
timeline.quote: Keranos's strike breached Xenagos's protections and actually touched the ground

citation.work: Theros eBook Godsend , Part 1: Sample Chapter
citation.text: "Theros eBook Godsend , Part 1: Sample Chapter". Uncharted Realms, Wizards of the Coast, 2 Apr 2014. Archived by the Internet Archive.

timeline.summary: Xenagos interrogates the oracle Kydele about the hydra, how to reach Nyx, and the edge of the world; she replies in riddles.
timeline.quote: "Is the hydra truly wandering among mortals?" Xenagos asked.

citation.work: Theros eBook Godsend , Part 1: Sample Chapter
citation.text: "Theros eBook Godsend , Part 1: Sample Chapter". Uncharted Realms, Wizards of the Coast, 2 Apr 2014. Archived by the Internet Archive.

timeline.summary: Kydele warns that the gods know something is amiss and that soon everyone will know Xenagos's name.
timeline.quote: "Soon everyone will know your name," she said.

citation.work: Theros eBook Godsend , Part 1: Sample Chapter
citation.text: "Theros eBook Godsend , Part 1: Sample Chapter". Uncharted Realms, Wizards of the Coast, 2 Apr 2014. Archived by the Internet Archive.

timeline.summary: Xenagos, weakened, lets Kydele transform into mist and escape toward Kruphix's Tree.
timeline.quote: so he did nothing as Kydele transformed into mist and vanished through the gap in the vine-roof

citation.work: Theros eBook Godsend , Part 1: Sample Chapter
citation.text: "Theros eBook Godsend , Part 1: Sample Chapter". Uncharted Realms, Wizards of the Coast, 2 Apr 2014. Archived by the Internet Archive.

timeline.summary: Ashiok reflects that turning an idea into a god is easy compared to Xenagos's feat, and that Cacophony could rise again.
timeline.quote: But turning an idea into a god was much easier.

citation.text: "Dreams of the City" by Ken Troop. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 23 Apr 2014.

timeline.summary: Raissa gives birth to her horned, kicking son, assisted by a midwife who thanks the gods.
timeline.quote: That anger gave her strength, which she used to finally expel him, howling, from her body.

citation.text: "Thank the Gods" by Clayton Kroh. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 30 Apr 2014.

timeline.summary: Raissa's flashback vision shows her son fully grown with horns, destined to be a king, with worlds beyond Theros spinning around him.
timeline.quote: Her son would be a king!

citation.text: "Thank the Gods" by Clayton Kroh. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 30 Apr 2014.

timeline.summary: Raissa decides not to abandon her child to Setessa as most satyr women would, believing he is special and needs her.
timeline.quote: This child was special, and he would need her to fulfill the destiny she had witnessed.

citation.text: "Thank the Gods" by Clayton Kroh. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 30 Apr 2014.

timeline.summary: Years later, Raissa escapes a burning house with her six-year-old son, who set her bed alight; they have been cast out of Setessa after he pushed a council member's son to his death.
timeline.quote: He had caused them to be cast out of Setessa when he shoved the son of one of the Karametra temple's ruling council to his death from a high rope bridge among the trees.

citation.text: "Thank the Gods" by Clayton Kroh. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 30 Apr 2014.

timeline.summary: Raissa, walking without destination, wonders whether she is punished for not paying tribute to the gods, and her son strikes her head with a stick.
timeline.quote: The boy struck her in the side of her head with his stick.

citation.text: "Thank the Gods" by Clayton Kroh. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 30 Apr 2014.

timeline.summary: Raissa returns with her son to the tidal pools and finds the starfish again.
timeline.quote: Together, Raissa and her son floated into the dream.

citation.text: "Thank the Gods" by Clayton Kroh. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 30 Apr 2014.

timeline.summary: In the vision the constellations of Nyx turn on Raissa's son with outrage and lightning, and he rises to meet them on a cloud of red and green power with a gleaming staff.
timeline.quote: outrage flared in their eyes

citation.text: "Thank the Gods" by Clayton Kroh. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 30 Apr 2014.

timeline.summary: The vision ends with Raissa's son laughing, holding aloft his stick with the impaled body of the starfish on it.
timeline.quote: At the end of the stick writhed the impaled gray body of the starfish.

citation.text: "Thank the Gods" by Clayton Kroh. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 30 Apr 2014.

timeline.summary: Elspeth and Daxos travel to Akros, where Xenagos tells her how to destroy the army by raising the river.
timeline.quote: they raised the river that ran through Akros and swept the army away

citation.text: "Daxos", section "Journey into Nyx". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Xenagos controls Elspeth, who kills Daxos while lashing out at the Phyrexian Obliterator in her memory.
timeline.quote: only realizing too late that she had just killed Daxos

citation.text: "Daxos", section "Journey into Nyx". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: In Nyx Elspeth strikes down Xenagos.
timeline.quote: They confronted Xenagos and battled the god until at last Elspeth struck him down

citation.text: "Elspeth Tirel", section "Journey into Nyx". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Supported by Ajani, Elspeth travels to Nyx and kills Xenagos.
timeline.quote: Supported by Ajani , Elspeth travels to Nyx and kills Xenagos .

citation.text: "Journey into Nyx", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Flashback: from Kruphix's Temple, Kydele watches Xenagos become a god and Elspeth, with Ajani, use Godsend to cut him from the sky.
timeline.quote: She saw Elspeth use the blade called Godsend to cut Xenagos from the sky.

citation.text: "Kruphix's Insight" by Kelly Digges. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 11 Jun 2014.

timeline.summary: Kruphix reveals that Theros is one of many worlds and that world-walkers like Elspeth, Ajani, Kiora and Xenagos have walked between them.
timeline.quote: So was the triton—the merfolk—Kiora, who called herself Callaphe and earned the ire of Thassa.

citation.text: "Kruphix's Insight" by Kelly Digges. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 11 Jun 2014.

timeline.summary: Kruphix explains that Xenagos traveled to godless worlds and tried to show everyone the gods were a lie, but people saw only chaos and he threatened nothing.
timeline.quote: decided everyone on Theros should know the gods were a lie.

citation.text: "Kruphix's Insight" by Kelly Digges. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 11 Jun 2014.

timeline.summary: Before Xenagos's rise, Kruphix declared the Silence of the Gods to restore balance after chaos in Nyx.
timeline.quote: Kruphix declared the Silence of the Gods

citation.text: "Kruphix", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kruphix and his oracle observed Xenagos's defeat by Elspeth and Ajani and Heliod's later betrayal of Elspeth.
